text: 2026-10-01 fsLR frame provenance research (advisory, no source changes). (1) ASSET IDENTITY, proven: TemplateFlow tpl-fsLR_den-32k_hemi-L_midthickness.surf.gii (sha256 036a8b6c...f1af) is byte-identical to the Van Essen lab Conte69 atlas v2 Conte69.L.midthickness.32k_fs_LR.surf.gii (GitHub mirror mgxd/brainplot). The GIFTI header: Caret 5.65, 2012-02-11, comment 'average of' 69 CH*/TT* subject midthickness.32k_fs_LR.coord.gii, external path MyelinMapping_Project/Conte69CommonFiles. TemplateFlow template_description credits Coalson/Glasser/Harms/Van Essen and cites doi:10.1093/cercor/bhr291 plus HCPpipelines global/templates. The GIFTI NIFTI_XFORM_TALAIRACH code with an identity matrix is a Caret default and not evidence. (2) VOLUME FRAME, strongly supported but not yet verbatim-quoted: Conte69 subjects were processed with the Glasser and Van Essen 2011 pipeline, with FNIRT nonlinear registration to FSL's MNI152, which is TemplateFlow MNI152NLin6Asym. HCP authors state that MNINonLinear surfaces are FNIRT-warped to the MNI template (hcp-users msg05000, msg05263). The PMC, JNeurosci and Europe PMC full texts were bot-blocked, so the methods sentence still needs retrieval for a verbatim provenance citation. One contradicting secondary source (netneurotools fetch_conte69 says 'MNI305') has no primary citation. (3) EMPIRICAL: a brain-mask geometry test over MNI152Lin, 2009cAsym, 6Asym, MNI305 and Colin27 cannot discriminate within the MNI family (fits within 2-4 mm); 6Asym is closest to identity, but this is weak evidence. The 09-23 GM-probseg test discriminates 6Asym from 2009c only. (4) Inherent limit: a group-average surface does not correspond to any single template's anatomy (Coalson, msg05000), so 'registration proof' is not attainable. The appropriate tier is publisher-declared frame with a methods citation.
